text:
Post mortem on marathon falling apart at mile 23: gels and hydration

Hi folks. I did my second marathon this past weekend and it didn’t go as well as I hoped. I started to deteriorate at mile 20 and completely fell apart at 23, though was able to finish. I think I got dehydrated and things started tightening up and prior muscle injuries flared up. It was warmer than expected and I overdressed a bit with ¾ running tights as opposed to my usual compression shorts. So, temperature comfort was a factor too.
My biggest takeaway was this: even if it’s the same exact course, no two marathons are the same. I can’t believe how different this year was compared to last year.
I think my issue was fueling and hydration, so I listed some questions below.
I tend to overthink things. My guess is I overcomplicated my approach and need to dial it back.
If my long runs are 20 miles, how do I train my stomach and, mostly, my mind to tolerate energy gels and electrolyte hydration after mile 23? I feel like the gels and stuff are just sitting and sloshing around. I take a gel every 20-30 min. My marathon pace was 4:25.
What is the advantage of isotonic gels (I use GU) if you need to be diligent about taking 4 oz of water with each one? Is it the smaller packaging?
3.  Do isotonic gels NEED to be taken with water? I use a mixture of Gatorade and Tailwind. Is that solution too concentrated to help absorb the gel? Details on hydration: 64 oz Camelback filled with a mixture of 24 oz Gatorade, 16 oz Tailwind, and water to top off to 64 oz. This lasts 13-15 miles, so for longer runs I stash a Gatorade somewhere along my route
4. I saw people doing the marathon around my pace without carrying extra fuel and hydration. The aid stations were every couple miles, sometimes 3 miles. And, at my pace (10 min miles) some stations ran out. Also, only 3 or 4 aid stations had UCAN gels. How do people go the distance with such little hydration and fueling? (Or, maybe they're the 75 who DNF).
Last year I took a gel every 30 min and had a much smoother marathon. I switched to more often after reading that we need 60-90 g carbs an hour.
I know they're convenient, but gels get expensive after a while. I've seen recipes for DIY, I think I need to explore some options to make gels for calories and use hydration for electrolytes

text:
I just ran my first marathon after ten months of training

I did it! After a lot of ups and downs, missed weeks thanks to knee pain, and so much self-doubt.
Last December a significant change happened in my life, and suddenly I had a lot of free time. I decided to use it to train for a marathon, which had been a long-awaited dream of mine.
When I started in January, the first milestone I set for myself was a half marathon at the end of March. I finished the half just a few minutes within the cutoff time, and I was thrilled. After that, I knew the next step was the marathon. I had almost 7 months to prepare, and I was dedicated.
I trained and trained: running 4 times a week, lifting 3 times, and cycling 1–3 times. I imagined my finish at least a hundred times.
Then came the long-awaited day, full of nerves and adrenaline, not knowing if I could even finish. Funny thing: the sweeper bus scared me in March, and last week too, even though my only goal was to finish within the cutoff time. I had a pace plan that I followed strictly., which worked out quite well, and so did my fueling.
After hours of running almost without stopping, I reached the last stretch, where my friends and family were waiting for me by the roadside. All the training, the missed parties, and the 4 am alarms in summer to avoid the heat flashed before my eyes, when I was crossing the finish line. It’s an incredible feeling to know you’re capable of something like that. I’ve been so happy ever since.
Honestly, looking back, I don’t even know how I did it. My longest run was 35k, and I planned my pacing and fueling based on that run.
edit: Some of you think I should not give advice to fellow beginners like me with my finish time so I deleted the recommendations
